text: Remember the Pacific Plate sliding down under the Mariana Plate a few centimeters a year?
As the plate bends into the trench, it cracks, seawater seeps into those cracks and soaks
into the rock, and then that wet rock is carried down with the plate, deep into the earth.
leaking? In a way, yes. And in 2018, scientists found it's leaking much more than anyone
thought. A team from Washington University in St. Louis placed 19 earthquake sensors
on the floor around the trench and listened to the earth's shake for more than a year.
From those vibrations, they could tell how deep the wet rock goes. Their answer? Almost
30 kilometers below the seafloor. They estimated that around the Mariana Trench, about 4 times
more water is being dragged into the Earth than earlier calculations said, and worldwide
through all these trenches, maybe 3 times more. So, when does the ocean run out?
